title: [R3-8 spinoff] The release handoff reads an activation-keyed artifact aggregate that no production writer ever writes
description:
FILED BY architect-fdbab575 2026-08-28 while re-planning task-06835dfad0aa4ecd9801d760fc559ee8 (R3-8). Measured by worker-4aba1617 during R3-8's step-1 writer audit (comment-68ea1ec0351a463985e05cbbe371c526) and independently ratified by the architect at HEAD ee36952e. Filed rather than absorbed because it is a REACHABILITY defect, not a fencing one, and R3-8 is a CRITICAL P1 fence row that must not grow a second subject.

THE FINDING. `release-handoff-classify.ts` ~:124 reads an artifact aggregate under an ACTIVATION-KEYED id. The only production writer of an artifact aggregate keys on `bound.target` instead (`foundation-attempt-store.ts` ~:237-243). The two ids are different, so the read can only ever observe an EMPTY aggregate. Nothing writes what this line reads.

WHY IT MATTERS, and why the honest answer is not obvious. An always-empty read is not automatically harmless — it depends entirely on what the classifier does with it, which is what this row must determine FIRST:
- If a present artifact would CHANGE the handoff classification, then the classifier has been taking the no-artifact branch unconditionally since the id diverged, and every handoff it built is missing a distinction it was designed to make. That is a live correctness defect and the fix is to correct the id.
- If the read only ever contributes an absent/empty value that the classifier already treats as the default, the line is dead weight and the fix is to DELETE it — removing a read that certifies nothing.
Do not guess between these. Measure the classifier's use of the value before choosing, and record the measurement.

WHY R3-8 DROPPED IT rather than fencing it: R3-8 fences seven aggregates as read-only decision legs so a commit cannot succeed if a source moved after it was read. Fencing an id that nothing writes fences nothing — it would add a leg against the MAX_DECISION_LEGS budget of 8 and certify a shape rather than a fact. R3-8's step 4 therefore drops the read from the release path and its completion comment records the drop; this row owns the underlying defect.

NOT IN SCOPE: the release fence itself (task-06835dfa), the finalizer version carriage (task-922c3b3d), and any change to `foundation-attempt-store.ts`'s writer keying — if the correct fix turns out to be moving the WRITER rather than the reader, that is a finding to report and re-scope, because that file has its own owners and its id derivation is load-bearing elsewhere.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK, recorded verbatim in a row comment: the divergence still exists at the delivered tree. Quote by file:line the id the classifier READS at release-handoff-classify.ts ~:124 and the id the writer WRITES at foundation-attempt-store.ts ~:237-243, and show they differ. Then prove the read is dead by execution, not by inspection: assert against a seeded store that the read returns empty for a realistic activation. If a writer for the read id now exists, ADOPT and close as fixed rather than re-implementing.

DECIDE AND RECORD WHICH DEFECT THIS IS, with the classifier's own code as the evidence: does a NON-EMPTY artifact aggregate change the handoff classification, or is the empty result indistinguishable from the default the classifier already takes? Drive both cases through the production classifier with a seeded store and quote the two outcomes. The answer selects the fix and must be written in a row comment before any production byte.

THE FIX MATCHES THE MEASURED ANSWER. If the artifact CAN change classification: correct the read to the id the writer actually writes, and an arm proves a written artifact now reaches the classifier and changes the outcome — a regression that has been silently taking the wrong branch. If it CANNOT: delete the read and the arm proves the classification is byte-identical before and after, so nothing depended on it. Do not do both, and do not leave the read in place with a comment explaining it.

MUTATION DRILL, one degree of freedom: re-introduce the divergent id (or re-add the deleted read) and prove the arm added above goes RED with its exact assertion. A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report in a comment, never a pass to bank — it would mean the new arm does not actually observe the behaviour it names. Restores proven by `git diff --exit-code` for tracked paths plus SHA256 against a %TEMP% backup in a call separate from the restore.

Gates standalone, foreground, unpiped, exit 0 with counts quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (quote the `$ tsc` echo) and a focused vitest run over the classifier's suite plus release-handoff-builder.test.ts. A bare `pnpm test` covers no apps/** and is not evidence. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus HEAD with an EMPTY owned-path intersection; production files at or under 400 lines; explicit-pathspec commit of the owned paths only; the completion comment names task-06835dfa as the row that measured and dropped the read.
taskRails: MEASURE BEFORE FIXING. The two candidate fixes — correct the id, or delete the read — are opposites, and choosing wrong either resurrects a dead branch or deletes a live one. The classifier's own use of the value decides it, and that measurement is DoD 2, not an implementation detail.

DO NOT change the WRITER's id derivation in foundation-attempt-store.ts. That file has other owners and its id derivation is load-bearing elsewhere; if the evidence says the writer is what is wrong, STOP and report for re-scoping rather than editing it here.

This row does NOT touch the R3-8 release fence (task-06835dfa) or the finalizer carriage (task-922c3b3d). If the fix appears to require either, that is a signal the scope boundary is wrong — report it.

An always-empty read is not proof of harmlessness. Prove the classification is unaffected by DRIVING both the empty and non-empty cases through the production classifier; reasoning about the code is not the evidence this DoD asks for.

Fail closed with exact code and layer where a refusal is involved; TDD; target <=250 lines per production source and split before 400; explicit-pathspec commits only, never `git add -A` and never a bare `git commit` — foreign WIP is live under apps/daemon/src/work.

(a) The divergence still exists: quote release-handoff-classify.ts:124 (deriveFoundationArtifactAggregateId(binding.activationAggregateId) inside the watch-ids roster, import at :22) and release-handoff-sources.ts:205 (readFoundationArtifactForAttempt with attemptAggregateId: binding.activationAggregateId, import at :27), versus the writer foundation-attempt-store.ts:237-243 keying sealFoundationArtifactRoster on bound.target. (b) Production consumer set of the two symbols, tests excluded, is still exactly {foundation-artifact-ledger.ts, classify.ts, sources.ts} — a fourth consumer is a stop-and-report.
(c) task-06835dfa is DONE (its fence has no ARTIFACT leg) and task-922c3b3d's owned paths do not overlap this row's.

(e) SHAPE SWEEP for R2: grep the classify/sources test suites for arms pinning the watch-ids roster's exact membership or length (toEqual/toHaveLength over the ids), and list every arm the roster shrink will red — those are in-scope repairs, not foreign red.

THE MEASUREMENT (DoD 2) — drive BOTH cases through the PRODUCTION classifier before any edit; this is what makes delete-vs-correct evidence rather than opinion, and it fixes successor task-e7b802bc's urgency.

(iii) VERDICT, recorded in a comment: if outputs are IDENTICAL in both cases, the reads are dead weight and deletion preserves behaviour — proceed. If the non-empty case CHANGES anything, the fix direction is unaffected (the id correction remains unsafe here per the human's ruling) but the successor's priority must be raised — say so in the comment, and if the change flows through a path OTHER than the two named reads, STOP and report because the dead-read premise itself is wrong.
Also capture the baseline `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` failing-path set for step 6's attribution delta; expect foreign red on this branch and disclose it by path, never edit it.

GREEN — THE DELETION (DoD 3, delete branch; the correct-the-id branch is routed to successor task-e7b802bc49734ee6a6ad7eb89579a106 by the DoD amendment comment).
(i) release-handoff-classify.ts: remove the deriveFoundationArtifactAggregateId(...) entry from the watch-ids roster at :124 and the now-unused import at :22.
(ii) release-handoff-sources.ts: remove the readFoundationArtifactForAttempt call at :205, its import at :27, and the plumbing that carried its always-ABSENT answer.
(iii) At EACH deletion site leave a two-line comment: the artifact read was activation-keyed while the sole writer keys on bound.target (dead since the divergence, executed witness in task-fdcfe1ca comment-a6f48882); the capability returns via task-e7b802bc49734ee6a6ad7eb89579a106 with the fence-or-immutability design. R4: a bare deletion reads as 'never meant to reach the handoff' — the comment is the durable pointer.
(iv) DO NOT touch: the writer (foundation-attempt-store.ts), the ledger, the harness seeding (seedArtifactManifest stays exactly as is — under deletion, seeded activation-keyed artifacts stay invisible to the handoff exactly as today), or any MAX_DECISION_LEGS/fence surface.
Step 3's arms flip: (i) and (iii) GREEN, (ii) STILL GREEN unchanged. Both production files shrink; re-quote their line counts (<=250 target).

MUTATION DRILL (DoD 4), one degree of freedom, restores proven by `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` in a call SEPARATE from the restore (all mutated paths tracked and clean).
D1: re-introduce the classify.ts roster entry (and its import) exactly as deleted -> the structural arm (step 3(i)) REDS on its exact set-membership assertion; the behaviour-preservation arm stays GREEN (the read was dead — behaviour never depended on it; that pairing is the whole story of this row). Restore, prove.
D2: re-introduce the sources.ts read -> the sources shape arm (step 3(iii)) REDS. Restore, prove.
D3 (guards the successor's mutant too): with the FIXED tree, seed an artifact at the DISPATCH key (the writer's real key) and re-run the classifier — output must be UNCHANGED, proving this row did not silently wire the corrected id without the atomicity design. If it changes, something else reads the dispatch key on the handoff path: STOP and report.
A GREEN drill where RED is required is a FINDING to report in a comment, never a pass to bank. Record mutant, command, exact red line and restore proof per drill in one comment.

GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT (DoD 5).
GATES standalone, foreground, unpiped, exit code + count lines quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (quote the `$ tsc` echo; sub-second green needs a planted-error control); focused vitest over release-handoff-classify.test.ts, release-handoff-sources.test.ts AND the consumer suites named in the fixture fan-out (release-handoff-builder.test.ts, attempt-release-disposition.test.ts, foundation-attempt-service.test.ts) — all must pass UNTOUCHED, which is itself evidence the deletion preserved behaviour for every consumer; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` graded by attribution: failing-path set at HEAD minus step 2's baseline, intersected with the six owned paths, EMPTY; foreign red disclosed verbatim by path.
REVIEW into a comment: does anything still reference deriveFoundationArtifactAggregateId outside the ledger and its tests (`git grep -n` at the delivered tree — expect ledger-only)? Is the harness seeding byte-identical (`git diff -- release-handoff-test-harness.ts` EMPTY)? Are the writer and fence surfaces untouched (`git diff -- foundation-attempt-store.ts attempt-release-fence-legs.ts` EMPTY)? Do both deletion-site comments cite task-e7b802bc?

Completion comment names successor task-e7b802bc49734ee6a6ad7eb89579a106 as the capability row (parked in BACKLOG pending the fence-or-immutability ruling) and quotes the step-2 verdict so the governor can set its priority.
